problem.title: Support-ticket routing
problem.context: A software company receives about 20,000 support tickets a day in English, Spanish and Portuguese, through e-mail and a web form. Tickets must reach one of 25 teams. First-line staff currently forward tickets by hand, and a misrouted ticket waits a day on average. Products and support teams change a few times a year.

requirements.text: Assign every new ticket to a team, and let a support agent move it to another team when the assignment is wrong.
Learn from the moves that support agents make.
At the daily peak of 3,000 tickets an hour, a ticket is assigned within 10 seconds of its arrival.
When a new team is created for a new product, at least 80% of the tickets meant for it reach it within two weeks.
Tickets may contain customers' personal data and must not leave the company's cloud region in the EU.

values: Ticket intake: Help desk webhook
Duplicate handling: Same customer and subject within one hour attaches to earlier ticket
Text representation: Pretrained multilingual sentence embeddings
Classifier: Logistic regression with one class per team
Agent correction: Help desk records agent-selected team
Agent explanation: Show two runner-up teams and influential words
Runtime: Managed Kubernetes in EU region with two replicas behind load balancer
Feedback training: Weekly Sunday retraining on last 90 days of final-team tickets
Evaluation gate: Replace model if last-week accuracy is at least current model
Embedding lifecycle: Embedding model remains fixed
Model distribution: Model file in object storage, loaded within five minutes
New-team cold start: Lead-written keyword rules until moves create training data
Monitoring: Per-team moved-ticket share with alert when share doubles week over week
points.description: Tickets arrive via the help-desk webhook, with recent same-customer/subject duplicates attached to the earlier ticket. Remaining tickets use fixed multilingual embeddings and one-class-per-team logistic regression; corrections feed weekly 90-day retraining, accepted models load from object storage into two EU Kubernetes replicas, and new teams initially use lead-written keyword rules while monitoring tracks moved-ticket shares. Trade-off: This provides multilingual coverage, rapid model rollout, redundancy, and some transparency, but weekly updates and fixed embeddings limit adaptation, while last-week accuracy can overlook per-team or new-team performance and keyword rules may be inconsistent.

points.description: A help desk webhook feeds tickets into a pipeline that attaches same-customer, same-subject tickets arriving within an hour to the earlier ticket. The system creates multilingual sentence embeddings, uses logistic regression to select a team, records the agent’s chosen team, and displays the two runner-up teams with influential words. Trade-off: This enables multilingual routing and simple team-level classification, but the deduplication rule may merge separate issues, and the model depends on team labels. Sentence embeddings also make “influential words” less direct to identify, weakening that explanation.

values: Runtime: Managed Kubernetes in EU region with two replicas behind load balancer
points.description: 1. A support-ticket routing service runs on managed Kubernetes in an EU region, with two replicas deployed behind a load balancer. The load balancer distributes requests between replicas and can continue serving if one replica fails. 2. Trade-off: This gains simpler cluster operations and basic replica-level availability, but incurs the cost of running two replicas. It remains vulnerable to an outage affecting the entire EU region and does not provide multi-region resilience.

points.description: 1. The help desk records the team chosen by agents, and each Sunday those final-team tickets from the last 90 days train the next model. A replacement is used when its last-week accuracy is at least the current model’s; the fixed embedding model is packaged in object storage for loading within five minutes, while monitoring alerts when a team’s moved-ticket share doubles week over week. 2. Trade-off: This provides simple, rapid model distribution and feedback-driven retraining, but adapts only weekly and cannot improve the fixed embeddings. The gate and monitoring emphasize aggregate accuracy and routing shifts, potentially overlooking other changes.

values: New-team cold start: Lead-written keyword rules until moves create training data
points.description: The system initially routes support tickets using keyword rules written by team leads. As tickets are moved to different teams, those moves accumulate as training data for improving or eventually replacing the rules. Trade-off: This provides an immediate, interpretable way to route tickets without historical data, but depends on leads maintaining useful keywords and may route unfamiliar wording poorly until enough corrective moves accumulate.

values: New-team cold start: Classifier alone until training examples arrive
points.description: The system uses the classifier as the sole basis for routing new-team tickets while no training examples are available. Once examples arrive, they can support a later transition to example-informed classification. Trade-off: This enables routing immediately without waiting for team-specific data. It gives up the reliability and adaptation that training examples could provide initially, increasing the risk of incorrect routing.

alternatives.name: Ticket routing as built
alternatives.summary: A webhook-driven multilingual classifier assigns teams, captures corrections, retrains weekly from final-team labels, and uses lead-written rules for new-team cold starts. It runs in the EU and rolls accepted model files out quickly.

choices.reason: A service needs ticket input to automate assignment, but a webhook is one implementation and no contrast establishes that it is required.
choices.solution_quote: The help desk tool sends every new ticket to the routing service through a webhook.

choices.value_id: Duplicate handling: Same customer and subject within one hour attaches to earlier ticket
choices.reason: Deduplicating can avoid repeated classification, but no requirement specifies this key or time window; the solution gives no evidence about false merges.
choices.solution_quote: It first looks for duplicates: if the same customer sent a ticket with the same subject in the last hour, the service attaches the new ticket to the earlier one and does not classify it.

choices.value_id: Text representation: Pretrained multilingual sentence embeddings
choices.reason: A multilingual representation supports the three ticket languages and may support a compact classifier, but neither the model choice nor its latency is compared with alternatives.
choices.solution_quote: Otherwise the service turns the subject and the body into an embedding with a pretrained multilingual sentence-embedding model

choices.value_id: Classifier: Logistic regression with one class per team
choices.reason: One class per team directly implements team selection and can be retrained from labels. The solution does not provide comparative accuracy, latency, or new-team evidence to settle this algorithm choice.
choices.solution_quote: and a logistic-regression classifier with one class per team picks the team.

choices.value_id: Agent correction: Help desk records agent-selected team
choices.reason: R1 requires agents to move a wrong assignment, and recording that move supplies the feedback required by R2.
choices.solution_quote: When an agent moves a ticket, the help desk tool records the new team.

choices.value_id: Agent explanation: Show two runner-up teams and influential words
choices.reason: The extra context may help an agent review an assignment, but R1 requires moving tickets and does not require runner-up teams or influential words.
choices.solution_quote: The service writes the team back to the help desk tool, with the two runner-up teams and the words that weighed most in the decision, which the tool shows to agents next to the ticket.

choices.value_id: Runtime: Managed Kubernetes in EU region with two replicas behind load balancer
choices.reason: The EU location is forced by C1, while managed Kubernetes, two replicas, and a load balancer are implementation choices. Their ability to meet Q1 is not established by measurements.
choices.solution_quote: The service runs on a managed Kubernetes cluster in the company's EU cloud region, with two replicas behind a load balancer.

choices.value_id: Feedback training: Weekly Sunday retraining on last 90 days of final-team tickets
choices.reason: Retraining on corrected labels answers R2. The weekly cadence and 90-day window are choices; no result shows that this pace meets Q2.
choices.solution_quote: Every Sunday a scheduled job exports the tickets of the last 90 days with their final teams, retrains the classifier

choices.value_id: Evaluation gate: Replace model if last-week accuracy is at least current model
choices.reason: The gate avoids deploying a model with lower measured last-week accuracy, but aggregate recent accuracy does not establish adaptation for a new team.
choices.solution_quote: and evaluates it on the last week's tickets. If it is at least as accurate as the current model, the job replaces the model file in object storage

choices.value_id: Embedding lifecycle: Embedding model remains fixed
choices.reason: Keeping embeddings fixed simplifies training and rollout, but no requirement dictates it and it limits one possible route for adapting representations.

choices.value_id: Model distribution: Model file in object storage, loaded within five minutes
choices.reason: Quick loading makes an accepted model available promptly, but no requirement directly states a deployment propagation target and it does not prove new-team accuracy.
choices.solution_quote: the job replaces the model file in object storage, and the service loads the new file within five minutes.

choices.value_id: New-team cold start: Lead-written keyword rules until moves create training data
choices.reason: Rules address the lack of training examples and are better supported than classifier-only cold start, but their measured coverage is absent and the specific rule method is not proven necessary.
choices.solution_quote: A new team has no training data until agents move tickets to it. Until then, keyword rules written by the team's lead route its tickets.

choices.value_id: Monitoring: Per-team moved-ticket share with alert when share doubles week over week
choices.reason: The dashboard can reveal teams with routing problems, including possible new-team issues, but it is an observation mechanism and does not itself learn from moves or guarantee the Q2 threshold.
choices.solution_quote: A dashboard shows, per team, the share of tickets that agents moved, and sends an alert when that share doubles from one week to the next.

adrs.title: Build an agent-correctable multilingual assignment path
adrs.context: Tickets need a team assignment and agents need a way to correct mistakes. The stated intake covers a multilingual service, and the tool can show agents the basis and alternatives for a decision.

options.name: Webhook, multilingual embedding classifier, and agent correction
values: Ticket intake: Help desk webhook
Duplicate handling: Same customer and subject within one hour attaches to earlier ticket
Text representation: Pretrained multilingual sentence embeddings
Classifier: Logistic regression with one class per team
Agent correction: Help desk records agent-selected team
Agent explanation: Show two runner-up teams and influential words
pros: Provides a concrete assignment path for multiple languages.
Records agent corrections for subsequent use.
Runner-up teams and influential words give agents context.
cons: The duplicate rule may attach a distinct issue to an earlier ticket.
The solution does not provide evidence that the displayed words explain the embedding-based classification.
options.reason: The assignment and correction functions directly answer R1. The specific webhook, representation, classifier, duplicate rule, and display choices are not shown to be forced.

adrs.title: Keep the service inside the EU region
adrs.context: Tickets can contain personal data and must remain in the company's EU cloud region. The service also has a stated peak-load latency target.

options.name: Two managed Kubernetes replicas behind a load balancer in the EU
values: Runtime: Managed Kubernetes in EU region with two replicas behind load balancer
pros: The service runs in the required EU region.
The load balancer distributes requests and replicas provide basic failover.
cons: The target of 3,000 tickets an hour within 10 seconds has no stated capacity test or measurement.
Two replicas do not protect against a region-wide outage.
options.reason: The EU location is forced by C1. Managed Kubernetes and two replicas are free implementation choices on the supplied evidence; their support for Q1 is plausible but unverified.

adrs.title: Turn agent moves into accepted classifier updates
adrs.context: Agent moves must inform learning. New products and teams arrive, so training and deployment need to make updated routing available, while new-team performance is important.

options.name: Weekly retraining with a recent-accuracy gate and rapid model loading
values: Agent correction: Help desk records agent-selected team
Feedback training: Weekly Sunday retraining on last 90 days of final-team tickets
Evaluation gate: Replace model if last-week accuracy is at least current model
Embedding lifecycle: Embedding model remains fixed
Model distribution: Model file in object storage, loaded within five minutes
Monitoring: Per-team moved-ticket share with alert when share doubles week over week
pros: Uses final-team labels from agent corrections for classifier retraining.
Checks candidate accuracy before replacing the current model.
Loads an accepted model within five minutes and monitors moved-ticket shares.
cons: Retraining is weekly and the embedding model is fixed.
A last-week accuracy comparison does not establish the performance of a new team.
No measured Q2 result is supplied.
options.reason: Recording and using agent moves fulfills R2. Weekly cadence, the 90-day window, aggregate gate, fixed embeddings, and distribution mechanism are implementation choices; they do not prove Q2, so they are not established as forced by its numerical target.

adrs.title: Provide a rule-based route before new-team examples exist
adrs.context: A new team has no training data until agents move tickets. It still needs tickets routed during the period in which examples are accumulating.

options.name: Lead-written keyword rules for cold start
values: New-team cold start: Lead-written keyword rules until moves create training data
pros: Allows routing before the new team has classifier training examples.
Rules can be inspected and maintained by the team lead.
cons: Rule coverage and accuracy are not reported.
The 80% within two weeks target remains unverified.
options.reason: The contrast with classifier-only routing shows that a no-example fallback is better supported for Q2, but the required threshold is not demonstrated, so this exact keyword-rule choice is not proven forced.

options.name: Use the classifier alone during cold start
values: New-team cold start: Classifier alone until training examples arrive
pros: Keeps routing on the existing classifier without a separate rule set.
cons: With no examples for the new class, it has no team-specific basis for meeting Q2.
options.reason: It continues to return a team but misses the new-team adaptation requirement in this evaluation, so the rule-based fallback is better supported.
